analyze: aliases-identities.summary:
Nobody sends as a second address today: not upstream, not the design. Upstream fixes From to {account.name, account.email} (lib/mail/smtp.ts:37-40). The send route accepts no From (app/api/accounts/[accountId]/smtp/send/route.ts:31-53). The compose From field is read-only (ComposeFields.tsx:340-346). Draft-send uses envelope.from = account.email (lib/drafts.ts:375-377). The design adds no sender identities and makes account.email immutable (TEAM-INBOX.md:126,370).

The "aliases" in upstream and in design §5.2 are recipient aliases, meaning address-book groups (lib/recipientAliases.ts, schema.ts:848). They have nothing to do with sender addresses. For those groups, viewer read, editor CRUD and manager replace-all import is reasonable.

What already works: sending from several real netcup mailboxes. Each Noctua account has its own SMTP login and appends to its own Sent folder (route.ts:165-175), so both members see a shared Sent folder. Design D4 lets an editor send in any mailbox they belong to. But compose cannot switch From across mailboxes.

The address counts suggest some MailPlus shared mailboxes are netcup aliases or forwards, not separate mailboxes. MonkeyDent has 5 shared mailboxes against 4 monkeydent.de addresses, and 8 shared plus 3 of the wife's own already exceed 10. If so, sender identities become necessary, and the address inventory must happen before go-live.

Reply never picks the address the mail was delivered to:
- Every "is it me" check compares only account.email (composeInitState.ts:175-177,307; drafts.ts:122-139).
- Delivered-To is not stored.
- Result: reply-all copies your own alias back in, and replies to imported Sent mail that went out from an alias are addressed to yourself.

When SMTP rejects a sender (nodemailer EENVELOPE), the error is not mapped (smtpError.ts:52-96) and surfaces as a generic 500.

Signatures:
- They are stored per mailbox, plain text only (useComposeController.ts:46-53), and only managers edit them (design §7.5).
- The design moves only defaultSignatureId into per-user prefs (§6.4). Each person signing with their own name in a shared mailbox therefore means duplicated signatures ("Kontakt – Paul", "Kontakt – Judith"). A {{user.name}} placeholder would avoid that.
- Reading the code (not run): opening compose only preselects the default signature and never inserts its text. Insertion happens only from the dropdown (ComposeMessageField.tsx:452-466), so the design's per-user default would have no visible effect unless Stage 3 fixes this.

Recommended order:
1. Runbook: inventory the addresses (mailbox, alias or forward) and test sending as an alias on netcup.
2. Stage 2: map sender rejections to a readable error, warn when the Sent copy could not be saved, and record who sent each message.
3. Stage 3 or a parallel branch feat/sender-identities: auto-insert the default signature, add signature placeholders, and build identities (team-level and manager-managed; reply auto-selects the address; all "is it me" checks use the identity set).

evidence: lib/mail/smtp.ts:37-40 and :49 — From is hard-coded to { name: account.name, address: account.email }; nodemailer derives MAIL FROM from it (no explicit envelope)

findings.details: Upstream: one From per Noctua account, period. Design: adds nothing and freezes account.email. Only workaround today is a second Noctua account with the same IMAP/SMTP login but the alias as email — that syncs the same IMAP mailbox twice into two shards (double storage/IMAP sessions), shows every message twice across the two accounts, and the design's admin/membership model would have to grant both. Not a real solution.
findings.proposal: New branch feat/sender-identities after feat/ui-shell merges (it touches smtp.ts, drafts.ts, smtp/send route, ComposeFields/ComposeOrchestrator). Store identities as team-level config: AccountSettings.identities = [{ id, address, name, signatureId?, replyTo?, envelopeFrom: 'identity'|'mailbox' }], editable only by manager (same gate as §5.2 'Account settings (team-level)', TEAM-INBOX.md:352). Send route and draft save accept identityId only (never free-text From) and validate it against the list; buildMailOptions(account, mail, identity) sets header From from the identity and envelope MAIL FROM per envelopeFrom; draft-send parses the stored draft's From, accepts it only if it is account.email or a configured identity, else falls back to account.email. Message-ID domain from identity address. Compose From becomes a Select (account address + identities). Add optional per-user defaultIdentityId to user_account_prefs (§6.4).

findings.details: The counts do not add up, so at least some MailPlus shared mailboxes are not separate netcup mailboxes (aliases/forwards into another mailbox, or MailPlus-internal). In Noctua a 'shared mailbox with common Sent' only exists if the address is its own IMAP mailbox. An alias delivering into another mailbox gives no separate inbox, no separate Sent, and (finding 1) no way to send as it.
findings.proposal: Runbook step before go-live: produce a table address → {netcup mailbox | alias of X | forward to X}, and target Noctua account + members/roles. Convert every MailPlus shared mailbox that needs its own inbox+Sent into a real netcup mailbox (netcup webhosting allows many mailboxes); the remaining aliases become identities (finding 1). On netcup, test per alias: send as alias via the mailbox's SMTP login (e.g. swaks --from alias --auth-user mailbox) and check SPF/DKIM alignment for cross-domain cases (e.g. advoria.de From through a monkeydent.de mailbox).

findings.details: Upstream and design: nobody does this. Effects today: a mail to kontakt-alias@ answered from the mailbox goes out as the primary address; reply-all CCs the alias (i.e. the mailbox itself); imported MailPlus Sent mail whose From is an alias is treated as 'not from me', so 'Reply' on it addresses the alias itself instead of the original recipient.

Auto-select identity on reply: first own address found in To, then Cc, then Delivered-To/X-Original-To (parse from the stored raw source on demand, or add a deliveredTo column at sync), else per-user/team default identity. Ship together with finding 1.

findings.details: Today this bites only if account.email is set to an address the SMTP login may not use (account.email and smtp.user are independent fields, AccountTabContent.tsx:69-73 vs :243). With identities it becomes the main failure mode. Note: Postfix sender-login checks act on the envelope sender (MAIL FROM), which nodemailer takes from `from`; that is why the identity needs an envelopeFrom option.

The design's answer for shared mailboxes (each person's own default via user_account_prefs) would therefore have no visible effect, and in a business it is easy to send unsigned mail.
findings.proposal: Verify in the running app. In Stage 3, when wiring effectiveSettings (prefs client resolution), call applySignatureToCompose(defaultSignature) at the end of openCompose for new/reply/forward, but not when reopening an existing draft (its body already contains the signature). Feed the per-user effective defaultSignatureId instead of MailClient.tsx:1973.

findings.details: By design it works only by duplication: a manager creates 'Kontakt – Paul' and 'Kontakt – Judith' in each of ~8 shared mailboxes (about 16 signatures to keep in sync), and each person picks a personal default. No signature per identity or alias. The codebase map's proposal of personal signatures (briefs/codebase-map.md:1896) was only partly adopted.
findings.proposal: Stage 3: add placeholder substitution in getSignatureBlocks (useComposeController.ts:46-53): {{user.name}}, {{identity.name}}, {{identity.address}}, filled from the session user (users.name, §3.1) and the selected identity. Then one team signature per mailbox renders per sender, with no schema change and no Stage 1 change. Add signatureId to identities (finding 1) and reuse applySignatureToCompose's swap logic (useComposeController.ts:57-111) when the identity changes.

findings.requirement: Recipient 'aliases' under the §5.2 role matrix
evidence: lib/db/schema.ts:848, :973-978 — recipient_aliases table keyed by accountId, unique name per account
lib/recipientAliases.ts:157-168, :251-356 — named recipient groups (name → recipient list); :358-398 — used for To/Cc autocomplete
lib/recipientAliases.ts:196-204 — transfer import DELETEs all aliases of the account, then inserts
doc/TEAM-INBOX.md:344, :350, :351 — read viewer; create/edit/delete editor; replace-all import manager
findings.details: Upstream 'aliases' are address-book distribution lists, not sender addresses. Per mailbox they are shared by both members, which suits a shared mailbox, and the roles are sensible: editors can add or change groups, and only managers can do the destructive replace-all import. Risk: if sender identities are later labelled 'Aliase' in the UI, someone may apply the §5.2 editor row to them by mistake. Identities change what goes out under the company's address and need SMTP verification, so they belong in the manager tier.
findings.proposal: Keep §5.2 as is. When identities are added, give them their own UI name ('Absenderadressen'/'Sender identities') and an explicit §5.2 row: use = editor (send), create/edit/delete/verify = manager.

findings.requirement: Recipients and the other member can tell which person sent from a shared mailbox
evidence: lib/mail/smtp.ts:37-40 — display name is account.name for every member
doc/TEAM-INBOX.md:416 and :459-460 — recordReplySent is called after send but is a no-op when the thread is unknown, so new outbound mail (not replies) gets no author record
briefs/codebase-map.md:1882 — an X-Noctua-Sent-By header would leak to recipients; draft-send uses one raw for wire and Sent copy
findings.details: MailPlus users rely on the signature to see who answered. In Noctua the Sent copy and the From line are the same for both people. The design records the author only for replies in known threads, through the activity log.
findings.proposal: Stage 2: also record outbound sends that start a new thread (create the thread state on first sync, or keep a small sent_log keyed by Message-ID with userId) so the shared Sent can show 'sent by'. Optional later: identity display-name template such as '{{user.name}} | MonkeyDent'. Do not add author headers to the wire copy.

findings.requirement: Sent copy reliably lands in the shared Sent folder after sending (from any identity)
evidence: app/api/accounts/[accountId]/smtp/send/route.ts:169-175 — APPEND to Sent wrapped in try/catch with '// ignore append failures', response still ok:true
lib/drafts.ts:387-398 — same for draft-send ('ignore append failure; caller still sees ok:true')
lib/specialFolders.ts:128-134 — findSentFolder matches by name only ('sent', 'sent items', …); if none matches, sentMailbox is null and no copy is stored at all
findings.details: Applies to upstream and design. netcup SMTP does not store sent mail, so this APPEND is the only route into the common Sent folder. If it fails, the mail went out but the other person never sees the reply, and nobody is told. Identities do not change this: the copy always goes to the account's Sent, which is the right behaviour for a shared mailbox.
findings.proposal: Stage 2 (owns smtp/send/route.ts and drafts.ts hook): return sentCopySaved:false plus a warning, show it in the existing compose notice, and log accountId/mailbox.

findings.requirement: Signature formatting suitable for business mail (links, logo, company legal details)

app/components/mailclient/composition/useComposeController.ts:46-53 — signature body escaped and turned into

; plain text only
app/components/account-settings/tabs/SignaturesTabContent.tsx:93 — edited in a plain TextArea

findings.details: Plain text covers the German legal footer, but MailPlus HTML signatures (logo, links) cannot be carried over 1:1; they have to be retyped as text.
findings.proposal: Later: allow markdown signatures and render them with markdownToEmailHtml for the HTML part, using the stripped text for text/plain. Not a go-live blocker.

findings.requirement: Every reply or new mail sent from a shared mailbox must end up in that mailbox's IMAP Sent folder (netcup does not save sent mail itself), and the user must find out when it does not
evidence: app/api/accounts/[accountId]/smtp/send/route.ts:165-175 (Sent folder looked up from the cached DB folder list; if none is found the APPEND is skipped, and any APPEND error is swallowed by `catch { // ignore append failures }`)
app/api/accounts/[accountId]/smtp/send/route.ts:194-202 (still returns ok:true; only sentMessageUid=null hints at a problem, and that value is the same when the server lacks UIDPLUS)
lib/drafts.ts:384-399 (draft-send path: same best-effort APPEND, errors swallowed)
app/components/mailclient/composition/ComposeOrchestrator.tsx:1022-1026 (shows the 'Email sent.' notice unconditionally); app/components/MailClient.tsx:3201 ('Draft sent.')
lib/mail/imap/folders.ts:21 createImapFolder is only called from app/api/accounts/[accountId]/folders/create/route.ts:32, so the send path never creates a missing Sent folder
lib/mail/imap/mutations.ts:36-55 appendImapMessage (single attempt, no retry)
findings.details: Upstream already does SMTP send plus IMAP APPEND to Sent with \Seen. It does not depend on the server saving a copy, which is right for netcup. But the copy is best-effort and fails silently in three cases: (a) the mailbox has no folder that findSentFolder recognises (for example a fresh netcup mailbox, or folders not listed yet for a newly added mailbox, because getFolders reads the DB cache at route.ts:165); (b) the APPEND throws (timeout, quota, connection drop); (c) the folder path is wrong. In every case the mail is delivered, the sender sees a success notice, and the other person never sees the reply in the shared mailbox. Nobody fixes this yet: the design (§6.3 reply hook, lines 459-460) adds only recordReplySent. This failure directly breaks the 'replies in a shared mailbox are visible to the other person' expectation.
findings.proposal: In smtp/send/route.ts and lib/drafts.ts sendDraftForAccount, return `sentCopy: 'appended' | 'failed' | 'no-sent-folder'`. Retry the APPEND once on a fresh connection. If no Sent folder is cached, call listImapFolders(account) (lib/mail/imap/folders.ts:16) before giving up. Log failures with accountId. In the UI, show a warning notice ('Sent, but no copy was saved to Sent; other members will not see it'), never a 'send failed' error, so nobody re-sends. Both server files belong to feat/thread-collaboration (§9 line 706), so do the server part in Stage 2. ComposeOrchestrator belongs to feat/ui-shell, which is running now, so the notice goes into Stage 3 (or a coordinated follow-up).

findings.requirement: After A sends a reply from a shared mailbox, B sees it in the conversation without needing to open the Sent folder
evidence: app/components/mailclient/composition/ComposeOrchestrator.tsx:980-1008 (only the sender's browser triggers the Sent-folder sync, with backfillUids)
app/components/mailclient/useSyncController.ts:495-525 (that sync swallows errors and returns null)
instrumentation.ts:3-13 (no server-side scheduled sync; sync is entirely client-driven)
app/api/accounts/[accountId]/imap/stream/route.ts:372-381 (IDLE watchers only on INBOX + active folder) and :31,384-448 (other folders only get a STATUS poll, default every 15 min)
app/components/mailclient/useSyncController.ts:1196-1225 (folder:update only updates counts, it never syncs or refetches)
lib/drafts.ts:262-273 (the draft-save path already ingests its APPENDed UID server-side via syncImapMessage + resolveThreadingForAccountMessages + upsertMessages; the send paths do not)
findings.details: Upstream: the shard DB is per mailbox and shared by all members, so once the Sent copy is synced, B sees it too. But only A's browser pulls it in, right after the send. If that sync fails, or the tab or detached compose window closes first, the reply stays on IMAP and is missing from Noctua's DB. It appears only when someone opens the Sent folder. Even when it works, B's open list or thread does not refresh, because no push exists between users and the STATUS poll changes only counters. The design adds no server-side ingest, so recordReplySent (§6.1 line 416) can resolve the thread only through inReplyTo/references.
findings.proposal: Stage 2 (feat/thread-collaboration owns smtp/send/route.ts and the lib/drafts.ts hook): after a successful APPEND with a uid, ingest the message server-side before responding, the same way drafts.ts:262-273 does: syncImapMessage(account, sentMailbox, uid) → resolveThreadingForAccountMessages → sanitizeSyncedMessage → upsertMessages, then recordReplySent. The reply is then in the shared shard regardless of A's browser. Stage 3: make B's thread view refetch on focus or on a lightweight 'thread changed' signal.

findings.requirement: Send from several addresses (aliases) and from the right shared address
evidence: lib/mail/smtp.ts:37-40 (From hard-coded to {account.name, account.email})
lib/mail/smtp.ts:70-80 and :106-111 (nodemailer derives MAIL FROM from that From, so the envelope sender is account.email)
lib/drafts.ts:375-378 (draft-send envelope.from = account.email)
app/api/accounts/[accountId]/smtp/send/route.ts:31-53 (the payload has no from field; the client value at ComposeOrchestrator.tsx:926 is only used for Reply-To, buildSendPayload.ts:82-88)
lib/data.ts:33-56 (Account has no identities/aliases; lib/recipientAliases.ts covers recipient groups, not sender identities)
doc/TEAM-INBOX.md has no identity/alias/From section (grep)
findings.details: Neither upstream nor the design supports more than one sender address per mailbox. Each Noctua mailbox sends only as its own address, with the display name account.name, which both members share. The user's counts point to a mismatch. MonkeyDent has five MailPlus shared mailboxes (Dev, EK, Kontakt, Rechnung, Store) but only 4 monkeydent.de addresses, and the personal addresses are presumably among those 4. So some shared mailboxes are probably aliases or forwards inside another netcup mailbox, not separate IMAP mailboxes. In Noctua, replies to mail arriving through such an alias would go out From the host mailbox's address. It also means aliases cannot be chosen at all, which was one of the needs behind the Google evaluation.
findings.proposal: Deploy runbook first: list which shared addresses are real netcup mailboxes and which are aliases or forwards. Where practical, turn each shared mailbox into its own netcup mailbox so 1 shared mailbox = 1 Noctua mailbox = 1 Sent folder. For true aliases, add `settings.identities: [{email, name}]` (manager-edited; no new auth because SMTP still uses the mailbox credentials). Add an optional `from` in the send/draft payload, validated server-side against account.email ∪ identities, and pass it to buildMailOptions and the envelope. Default to the identity matching the original To/Cc on reply. Confirm netcup SMTP accepts alias From addresses for the authenticated mailbox. Not owned by any Stage 1 branch; schedule after Stage 2 or as its own branch.

findings.requirement: Drafts in a shared mailbox are safe when both people open or send the same reply
evidence: lib/drafts.ts:204-279 (drafts are IMAP-APPENDed to the mailbox's Drafts folder with \Draft \Seen and upserted into the shared shard, so they are visible to and editable by both; §5.2 line 349 gives editors 'drafts, send')
lib/messageIds.ts:26-30 (row id = hash of the Message-ID; drafts.ts:225-236 keeps the Message-ID across saves, so both editors address the same row)
lib/drafts.ts:246-255 (each save deletes the previous IMAP UID and local row, then APPENDs: last writer wins silently, and a failed APPEND after the delete loses the server copy)
app/api/accounts/[accountId]/drafts/[draftId]/discard/route.ts:43,66-68 and ComposeOrchestrator.tsx:958-965 (A's send discards the draft row)

lib/drafts.ts:225-226 (B's next autosave finds no existing draft, so preservedMessageId is undefined and a new draft with a NEW Message-ID is created, which the old-Message-ID tombstone does not block)
findings.details: Visibility works as the user wants: drafts live on IMAP, are shared, and other IMAP clients see them too. Concurrency is unprotected. If A and B both have the same draft open, their autosaves overwrite each other with no warning, and racing saves can leave two drafts. Worse, after A sends, B's still-open compose window recreates the draft under a fresh Message-ID, and B can send a second reply to the customer. Upstream has no version check, and the design adds none.
findings.proposal: Stage 2: add optimistic concurrency to POST drafts/save. The client sends the imapUid (or a server-issued revision) it last saw. If the stored draft row has a different imapUid, or the row is gone or tombstoned, return 409 'This draft was changed or sent by someone else'. Stage 3: on 409, show the message and offer 'reload draft' or 'save as new draft'. Also APPEND the new version before deleting the old UID (drafts.ts:246-255) so a failed APPEND cannot lose the draft.

findings.requirement: Warn when someone else is already replying to the same conversation
evidence: Grep for presence/'replying'/lock in app/ and lib/ finds nothing relevant; TEAM-INBOX.md has no such feature (§6, §7.3 lines 640-656 only cover assignee, status, comments, activity)
app/components/mailclient/composition/ComposeOrchestrator.tsx:899-902 (a reply or forward auto-saves a draft on open)

analyze: shared-sent.summary:
Repo root for all paths: /home/monkey/.t3/scratch/2026-10-22-https-github-com-paulwellnerbou-noctua-8f78a215/noctua-mail (branch team-inbox).

What upstream already does: Noctua stores sent mail itself, without relying on the server. After the SMTP send it APPENDs the message to the Sent folder with \Seen (smtp/send/route.ts:138-175; lib/drafts.ts:375-399). The INBOX. prefix is handled: folder ids carry the full path and matching uses the leaf name (mailbox.ts:20-37, mailboxPaths.ts:3-8). Sent folder names in German and English are recognised (specialFolders.ts:22-35). SMTP logs in with the mailbox's own credentials (smtp.ts:70-80). From and envelope sender are always account.email, with display name account.name (smtp.ts:37-40). Replies join the conversation thread through Message-ID/In-Reply-To/References (lib/threading.ts), and cross-folder threads are on by default. Drafts are stored in the mailbox's IMAP Drafts folder and in the shared shard DB, so both members can see, edit and send them.

What breaks or weakens "replies in a shared mailbox are visible to the other person":
1. The Sent copy is best-effort and fails silently. A missing Sent folder or a failed APPEND still produces the "Email sent." notice.
2. The Sent copy only gets into the shared DB through the sender's browser sync right after sending. There is no server-side ingest. The other person's view updates live only for INBOX and the active folder, so they may not see the reply until someone opens Sent.
3. The draft-send path never sets \Answered on the original message.
4. findSentFolder ignores the \Sent special-use flag. It works today mostly because the server lists special-use folders first.

Draft collisions are real. Concurrent saves overwrite each other silently (last writer wins). After one person sends, the other's open compose window recreates the draft under a new Message-ID, which allows a second reply to the customer. Nothing in upstream or the design warns "someone else is replying".

Sending from aliases is not possible: only one From per mailbox, and the design adds nothing here. The user's numbers (5 MonkeyDent shared mailboxes but only 4 monkeydent.de addresses) suggest some MailPlus shared mailboxes are aliases rather than real netcup mailboxes. That needs an inventory, and either separate netcup mailboxes or a sender-identity feature.

The design's only addition in this area is recordReplySent (§6.3, a no-op when the thread is unknown). Most fixes belong in Stage 2: feat/thread-collaboration already owns smtp/send/route.ts and the lib/drafts.ts hook. UI notices go into Stage 3, because ComposeOrchestrator belongs to feat/ui-shell, which is in progress. The deploy runbook must check per mailbox: CAPABILITY (UIDPLUS, SPECIAL-USE), LIST (folders and flags), where the MailPlus sent-history import lands, and netcup forwards into personal mailboxes.

findings.details: Upstream, unchanged by the design: each visible tab holds 1-2 long-lived IDLE connections on its active mailbox. On top come a transient STATUS poll every 15 min, 1 pooled interactive connection (more under concurrency), and 1 per running sync worker. Each folder or mailbox click costs 1-2 new IMAP logins. Household estimate with 2 users on desktop + phone: steady state is about 2-8 connections in total, concentrated on 1-4 mailboxes. The other 8-10 mailboxes get none, which is the problem in finding 1. Worst case on one shared mailbox: both users with 2 visible tabs each in a non-INBOX folder, during a sync and a mutation: 4x2 IDLE + 1 pooled + 1 worker + 1 fresh = about 11. That exceeds Dovecot's default mail_max_userip_connections=10, and all of these connections come from the same server IP. netcup's actual limits are unknown. With the proposed watcher, steady state is 12 IDLE connections in total (1 per mailbox login) plus transient ones. If the stream reuses the watcher's INBOX events, each mailbox stays at or below about 3-4.
findings.proposal: Deploy runbook: before go-live, measure netcup's per-mailbox and per-IP concurrent IMAP limits and its login rate limit with a small script that opens N sessions to one mailbox. analyze: many-mailboxes.summary:
Upstream sync works only from the browser and only for the active account. Nothing runs on the server (instrumentation.ts:3-13). The IDLE stream, polling, startup sync and notifications all follow activeAccountId (useSyncController.ts:909-967,1189; MailClient.tsx:4112-4180). The design keeps that model: the §1 non-goal plus sync triggered by viewers (§5.2). So with about 12 mailboxes, any mailbox not open in some tab is never synced and has no unread count and no notification. Nobody, neither upstream nor the design, provides a server-side watcher, badges for non-active mailboxes, or notifications for them. That is the main gap for replacing MailPlus.

Connections, today's model: each visible tab holds 1-2 IDLE connections on its active mailbox, plus a 15-min poll connection, a pooled connection and a sync-worker connection. Every folder or mailbox click logs in again. Worst case is about 11 connections on one shared mailbox when both users are on it from 2 devices, which exceeds the Dovecot default of 10 per user+IP. netcup's real limits must be measured. A server watcher would hold 12 steady IDLE connections, one per mailbox, and should feed the tab streams. Sync workers are Bun subprocesses with no global cap, so 12 can run at once during a burst or the initial import. Shard DBs are cheap (lazy open, closed after 5 min idle).

Switching between 12 mailboxes is workable but cold every time: about 8-10 requests, 1-3 IMAP logins, and all state is reset.

Two design or ordering bugs matter for this household:
1. The account order is effectively random (ORDER BY a sha256-based id), and there is no grouping. The two 'Dev' mailboxes would be indistinguishable.
2. §5.3 `shared` uses `ownerUserId !== viewer`, and admin-created mailboxes have ownerUserId=null. So the wife's admin-provisioned personal mailboxes would show up under 'Shared'.

Recommendation:
- Stage 1 now: the ui-shell sidebar groups by organisation, derived from the e-mail domain with an optional label, sorted, collapsible, with a badge slot. team-auth fixes the `shared` flag.
- Stage 2: a new parallel branch feat/mailbox-watcher with one server IDLE per mailbox INBOX that triggers 'new' syncs, a global worker cap, GET /api/me/mailboxes/summary and a per-user SSE /api/me/events.
- Stage 3 must: unread plus assigned/open badges for every mailbox, notifications for non-active mailboxes with per-user mute, and account-scoped keys everywhere.
- Stage 3 should: a read-only cross-mailbox 'Assigned to me' list that switches mailbox and jumps on click (server fan-out over at most 12 shards, roughly 1-2 days).
- Later: Web Push and the fully interactive unified inbox (activeAccountId is threaded through about 30 client modules).
- Deploy runbook: measure netcup's connection and login limits, and import the history one mailbox at a time.

Use explicit Sent mapping (--automap/--f1f2), --useheader Message-Id with --addheader, and --exclude for the shared namespace, and never use --delete1 or --delete2. Map each MailPlus shared mailbox to its own real netcup mailbox and one Noctua account, because upstream sends only as account.email and keeps Sent per IMAP account (lib/mail/smtp.ts:33-40, smtp/send/route.ts:166-171). The biggest risk is MailPlus POP3 fetch. Noctua copies the netcup IMAP state and deletes whatever disappears from it (imap/stream/route.ts:323-336, syncOperation.ts:456-460). Non-INBOX folders can be copied in advance while MailPlus is still live. MX already points to netcup, so cut-over needs no DNS change. Rollback works because imapsync only copies, but POP3 may only be re-enabled after the imported mail is removed from the netcup INBOX. Several points are unverified: how MailPlus exposes shared mailboxes over IMAP, what the POP3 keep/delete option is called, and netcup's IMAP connection limit. The runbook checks each of them with dry runs. Everything here belongs in the deploy runbook (nobody has written it yet; the design has no migration section). analyze: fit-critic.summary:
TEAM-INBOX.md is a collaboration and UI design: login, roles, assignment and comments, the new shell. It is not a plan for replacing MailPlus. It never mentions MailPlus, netcup, import, aliases or a shared Sent folder, and §9 ends at feat/collab-ui with no cutover stage. Topics other analysts cover in depth, one line each: shared/common Sent (not designed), sending from aliases (not designed), ~12 mailboxes with one-active-at-a-time sync (not designed), history import including sent mail (not designed), IMAP-mailbox login (open under the Better Auth pivot).

The most important gap beyond those is new-mail notifications and unread indicators across all mailboxes. Upstream watches and notifies only the active mailbox in an open tab (useSyncController.ts:909-956). There is no server scheduler and no Web Push (public/sw.js:225-233), and the designed sidebar shows no unread counts (TEAM-INBOX.md:605-606). Without this, mail to kontakt@ or rechnung@ goes unseen until someone switches mailboxes. Proposed for Stage 2: server-side INBOX polling for all accounts, a mailbox-summary endpoint and sidebar badges; Web Push later.

Other must-haves are mostly deploy-runbook work:
- **Backup:** online `VACUUM INTO` copies of mail.db and the shard DBs, plus the env keys. After cutover the comments, assignments and topics exist only there, and Noctua's source cache is not a mail backup, so the netcup mailboxes need an independent mail backup before MailPlus goes off.
- **Spam:** netcup's per-mailbox Plesk filter, set to move spam to the Spam folder, replaces MailPlus filtering. Noctua only moves mail to Junk manually and reads no X-Spam headers.
- **Auto-replies and rules:** inventory the MailPlus auto-replies and rules, then recreate them in netcup Plesk. Noctua has no vacation or rules feature, and ManageSieve on netcup is unverified.
- **Attachment limits:** send and draft-save carry base64 JSON, so an nginx default `client_max_body_size` of 1 MB breaks attachments over about 700 KB. netcup's SMTP SIZE limit still needs checking.

Two must-haves sit in the stages:
- **Per-person signatures (Stage 3):** the design's per-user signature default misses DetachedComposeWindowClient.tsx:413. It also needs one signature per person in each of the 8 shared mailboxes, unless {{user.name}} placeholders are added.
- **Mobile (Stage 1):** the layout is designed (D11, §7.2), but a real-device PWA acceptance test on both phones is missing.

Nice-to-haves for later:
- **Cross-mailbox search:** per-mailbox FTS5 search exists; searching all mailboxes at once is a non-goal.
- **Contacts:** there is no address book. Autocomplete uses only the last 2000 messages of the active mailbox; Synology Contacts can stay on the NAS.
- **Calendar:** CalDAV is supported per mailbox, but the SSRF guard rejects a Synology Calendar reached by a LAN IP or split-DNS name.
- **Labels:** IMAP folders are fine. Topics work as labels but live only in the Noctua DB, and MailPlus labels are not imported.

The netcup facts (two spam-filter layers, the Plesk autoresponder) come from netcup's help pages: https://www.netcup.com/en/helpcenter/documentation/web-hosting/setup-spamfilter and https://helpcenter.netcup.com/en/wiki/web-hosting/email-setup-manage. ManageSieve availability and the netcup message-size limit are unverified.

findings.requirement: Make IMAP login against the person's own mailbox a first-class path, and replace the 'exactly one member' rule with an eligibility check under which shared mailboxes can never authenticate anyone
evidence: doc/TEAM-INBOX.md:39 (D3: IMAP login is kept only as a migration path, only for mailboxes the user owns alone)
doc/TEAM-INBOX.md:256-262 (§4.2 step 4: candidates are filtered by `email === typed || imap.user === typed`, `ownerUserId === user.id`, and exactly one member)
doc/TEAM-INBOX.md:370-375 (§5.3: a change of imap.host/user is verified against the NEW endpoint; relogin still accepts a different imap.user when a password is supplied)
app/api/accounts/[accountId]/relogin/route.ts:26-51 (upstream relogin rewrites imap.user and the password after checking them only against the current host)
app/api/auth/login/route.ts:36-39,65-69 (upstream finds the account by address, imap.user or link, then takes the identity from ownerUserId ?? first link ?? account.id)
lib/accountId.ts:3-7 (account id = sha256 of the lowercased address, so there is at most one account per user e-mail)
lib/mail/imapClientOptions.ts:496 (imap.secure is passed straight to ImapFlow; with secure:false STARTTLS is not enforced)
findings.details: Upstream: login works only through IMAP, and the identity comes from the account row (login/route.ts:65-69). The design removes that and keeps IMAP only as a legacy path. Is 'exactly one member' needed? Here are the household cases. (a) kontakt@ has its own netcup credentials. No users row has that address, so step 1 already refuses. The spouse typing her own e-mail plus kontakt@'s password fails because kontakt@'s address does not match hers. Owner-less admin mailboxes fail the ownerUserId check. (b) A shared mailbox the user owns (kontakt@ owned by him): its address is not his e-mail, so it is never a candidate. (c) His personal mailbox shared read-only (viewer or editor) with the spouse: she cannot edit the row (§5.2), so the member rule protects nothing. It only locks him out of IMAP login the moment he shares the mailbox. If he has no app password and is the only admin, nobody can administer the install any more (recovery only by editing the DB). (d) His personal mailbox shared with the spouse as MANAGER: this is the only case the rule actually protects under the current check. account.email cannot be changed and keeps matching his typed e-mail. A manager, however, can relogin with a different imap.user (her own mailbox) or PUT an imap.host she controls (verified against that same host). After that, his e-mail plus her password logs in as him. So the rule is only needed because the check itself is too loose: `email OR imap.user`, any host, any TLS mode. The fix is to tighten the check instead. The only candidate is the single account `accountIdFromEmail(user.email)`, and it must have ownerUserId = user.id, lower(email) = user.email AND lower(imap.user) = user.email, imap.secure = true, and an imap.host on an operator allowlist. A successful check then proves that the person has their real mailbox password at the real provider, no matter who can edit the row, and the member count stops mattering. Making endpoint edits on a login mailbox owner-only is still worth doing, but it prevents a co-manager from switching off the owner's login (denial of service), not impersonation. No DDL change is needed; the schema already committed in Stage 1 (per the brief) stays as it is.
findings.proposal:
D3 OLD: "Legacy IMAP login stays only as a migration path for a user row without a password hash, and only for mailboxes that user alone owns (§4.2). It never resolves a session user from an account." NEW: "Mailbox (IMAP) login is a first-class login method next to the optional app password. A user can sign in with the password of their login mailbox: the one account with `ownerUserId = user.id`, `lower(email) = lower(imap.user) = user.email`, `imap.secure = true` and an `imap.host` listed in `NOCTUA_IMAP_LOGIN_HOSTS` (unset or empty = mailbox login off). The number of members does not matter. Login never takes the session user from an account; shared mailboxes are not owned by a user under that user's own address, so they never authenticate anyone." Rationale column, append: "Binding the login to the user's own address plus an operator host allowlist means a successful login proves the person has their real mailbox password; nobody who can edit the account row can redirect the check."
§3.1 OLD comment "-- argon2id; NULL = legacy IMAP login only" NEW "-- argon2id app password, optional; NULL = mailbox (IMAP) login only"; OLD "-- unix seconds; sessions with iat < this are invalid" NEW "-- unix seconds; bumped by app-password changes and by stored-password changes of the login mailbox; sessions and MCP tokens with iat < this are invalid".
§4.2 NEW (replaces the whole body): "Body `{ email, password, preferredAccountId? }`. Same-origin JSON check (§4.6). Rate limits: per IP as today; per e-mail 5/min for every attempt in either branch; and a mailbox-login limiter that is checked only right before an IMAP verification (10 per 15 min per e-mail, 30 per hour in total). When the mailbox-login limiter is exhausted, step 4 is skipped (no IMAP connection); the app password still works and the response stays the generic 401.
1. `email = lower(trim(email))`. Load the auth row (`getUserAuthByEmail`): `{ id, role, passwordHash, disabledAt, mustChangePassword }`. No row → 401 without any IMAP connection, including when the users table is empty (a new install is bootstrapped only through the admin invite code and §4.3).
2. Disabled user, or any failure below → `401 { ok:false, message:"Invalid email or password" }`. This is the only failure response besides `400 Missing credentials` and `429`.
3. App password: if `passwordHash` is set and verifies (argon2id), set `amr = "password"` and continue with step 5.
4. Mailbox login (no hash, or the hash did not verify): `L = getLoginMailbox(user)` (lib/accountAccess.ts) is the account with `id = accountIdFromEmail(user.email)` if all of these hold, otherwise none: `teamFeaturesSupported()`; `ownerUserId === user.id`; `lower(trim(email)) === user.email`; `lower(trim(imap.user)) === user.email`; `imap.secure === true`; `imap.host` matches `NOCTUA_IMAP_LOGIN_HOSTS` (comma-separated exact hosts or `*.suffix`). The number of members and their roles do not matter. No `L`, or limiter exhausted → 401 without an IMAP connection. Otherwise call `verifyImapCredentials(L, password)`; false (wrong password or server unreachable: logged differently, answered identically) → 401. On success set `amr = "imap"`. Write-back: if the typed password differs from the stored `L.imap.password`, one immediate transaction sets `imap.password`; sets `smtp.password` only when `lower(smtp.user) === lower(imap.user)` and the stored SMTP password equalled the old IMAP password or was empty; and sets `users.passwordUpdatedAt = now`. Write-back happens only here, only after a successful verification, and never touches any other account. An account the user only belongs to is never a candidate.
5. Accessible accounts = `listAccessibleAccountsForUser(user.id)` (owned first, then by name). `accountId` = `preferredAccountId` if accessible, else `L.id` after a mailbox login, else the first one, else undefined. Session `{ userId: user.id, role, amr, accountId, iat: now, exp }`, using the same `now` as the write-back. Response `{ ok:true, accountId: string | null, mustChangePassword }`. The `ownerUserId`/first-linked/`account.id` fallbacks are deleted.
6. Rotate: every successful login issues a fresh `iat`."
§5.3, append after "...unless the password is provided for it.": "If the account is currently some user's login mailbox (§4.2 step 4), changes to `imap.host|port|secure|user` are owner-only (403 `{ code: \"login_mailbox_owner_only\" }` for other managers). Any change of its stored IMAP password (PUT, relogin, `POST /api/accounts` on the existing id) bumps the owner's `passwordUpdatedAt`; if the caller is the owner, their cookie is re-issued with a fresh `iat`."

findings.details: Neither upstream nor the design revokes anything when the netcup password changes. The stored password becomes stale, sync fails with reauthRequired and the client shows the relogin dialog. Meanwhile every live Noctua session and MCP token of that person stays valid as long as a tab keeps polling /me. So for someone who signs in with the mail password, changing a leaked netcup password does not evict an attacker who already has a Noctua session; the attacker can keep reading the cached mail. Two small fixes need no server-side state. (1) Treat the login-mailbox password as a login credential: any change of its stored IMAP password (login write-back, relogin, PUT, POST on an existing id) bumps the owner's passwordUpdatedAt. The existing D5 check then kills older sessions and MCP tokens, and the caller's cookie is re-issued if the caller is the owner. The upstream relogin dialog then repairs the stored password and revokes old sessions in one step. (2) Sessions created by mailbox login carry `amr: "imap"` and have a maximum age counted from iat. That limits the exposure when the person changes the netcup password but does not open Noctua afterwards. Side effect to document: a netcup password change also invalidates that user's MCP tokens, the same as an app-password change does.
findings.proposal:
D5 OLD: "Sessions and MCP tokens carry `iat`. Every guard loads the user row and rejects disabled users, missing users, and sessions issued before `passwordUpdatedAt`." NEW: "Sessions and MCP tokens carry `iat`; sessions also carry `amr` (`password` | `imap`). Every guard loads the user row and rejects disabled users, missing users, and sessions issued before `passwordUpdatedAt`. `passwordUpdatedAt` is bumped by every app-password change and by every change of the stored password of the user's login mailbox (login write-back, relogin, PUT), so changing the mail password at the provider and signing in once evicts every other session and MCP token. Mailbox-login sessions have a maximum age." (the remaining sentences of D5 stay)
§4.1 OLD: "`SessionData` gains `iat: number` (unix seconds). Password logins never set `imap`/`smtp`." NEW: "`SessionData` gains `iat: number` (unix seconds, the authentication time; `refreshSession` never changes it) and `amr: \"password\" | \"imap\"`. Logins never set `imap`/`smtp`."
§4.1 OLD: "...and returns 401 when the user row is missing, `disabledAt` is set, or `iat < passwordUpdatedAt`." NEW: "...and returns 401 when the user row is missing, `disabledAt` is set, `iat < passwordUpdatedAt`, or `amr === \"imap\"` and `now > iat + NOCTUA_IMAP_SESSION_MAX_AGE_SECONDS` (default 604800). For `amr: \"imap\"` sessions, `/api/auth/me` never sets `exp` past that limit. MCP tokens are not subject to the maximum age; they die on a `passwordUpdatedAt` bump."

analyze: imap-login.summary:
Recommendation: make mailbox (IMAP) login a first-class login method and keep app passwords as an optional extra. This needs no DDL change: the schema already committed for Stage 1 (per the brief) stays as it is, and the changes sit in files owned by feat/team-auth (lib/accountAccess.ts, lib/auth.ts, app/api/auth/**, app/api/admin/**) plus copy in §7.4 owned by feat/ui-shell.

**Is "exactly one member" needed?** Not if the check is tightened. Today it is needed only because the check is loose: `email OR imap.user`, any host, any TLS mode. With that, a co-manager of the owner's personal mailbox could relogin with another imap.user, or PUT an attacker-controlled host (verified against itself), and sign in as the owner (doc/TEAM-INBOX.md:256-262, 370-375; relogin/route.ts:26-51). Replace the member rule with a stricter check:
- The only candidate is the account `accountIdFromEmail(user.email)` (lib/accountId.ts:3-7).
- Its owner must be the user (ownerUserId = user.id).
- Both `lower(email)` and `lower(imap.user)` must equal the user's e-mail.
- `imap.secure` must be true.
- The host must be on an operator allowlist (`NOCTUA_IMAP_LOGIN_HOSTS`).

A successful login then proves the person has their real netcup password. The shared mailboxes (kontakt@ and the others, whether owned by him or by nobody) and a personal mailbox shared with the spouse can never authenticate anyone. Dropping the rule also removes a lockout: today, an admin without an app password locks himself out the moment he shares his personal mailbox.

**Other changes needed:**
- **Bootstrap:** delete the legacy branch 4(b), which cannot work as written. The upstream admin invite code (schema.ts:690-694) already handles bootstrap.
- **Signup:** the app password becomes optional only with a qualifying mailbox. Signup must also return 409 for an existing mailbox, because upstream and the design overwrite an existing account row and its owner (rowParsers.ts:165).
- **Setting an app password:** require the current password (app or mailbox password). Today a user without an app password can set one with no proof, which lets someone holding a session plant a permanent second login.
- **Admin provisioning:** `POST /api/admin/accounts` accepts an optional `ownerUserId`. Otherwise an admin-created user without a password has no way to sign in.
- **Write-back:** after a successful mailbox login, write the new password into the stored IMAP password. Copy it to SMTP only when the SMTP user is the same and the old passwords matched (upstream copies it blindly, login/route.ts:47-58).
- **Revocation:** every change of the stored login-mailbox password bumps `passwordUpdatedAt`. Mailbox-login sessions get `amr: "imap"` and a 7-day maximum age, because `/api/auth/me` otherwise extends sessions forever (me/route.ts:26-29). Today nothing revokes sessions after a netcup password change.
- **Rate limits:** the per-e-mail limiter covers both branches, plus a dedicated limiter for IMAP checks, since every attempt is a real netcup LOGIN from the server IP.

**Alternatives.** "IMAP only" would remove D1/§4.4, the mustChangePassword handling and about 8 tests. In exchange, login depends on netcup being up (imapAuth.ts:36-37), there is no fallback login or admin reset, and Stage 1 work would be undone. Not recommended. "Leave as is" is safe, but nobody new can reach mailbox login (signup requires an app password, §7.4 has no mailbox fields, admin mailboxes have no owner), so both spouses would end up with app passwords anyway. The bootstrap, signup and app-password issues above need fixing either way.

findings.details: Small correction: imapflow can return a uid without UIDPLUS, but only when the destination mailbox is the one currently selected. missedByAnalyst: Calendar RSVP Sent copy has the wrong Message-ID. sendSmtpMessage compiles the message twice (lib/mail/smtp.ts:106-107: once for sendMail, once for the raw APPEND), and the respond route passes no messageId (app/api/accounts/[accountId]/calendar/events/[eventId]/respond/route.ts:130-143). nodemailer generates a random Message-ID per compile (node_modules/nodemailer/lib/mime-node/index.js:922-927), so the Sent copy differs from what the organizer received, and the organizer's replies will not thread with it. Fix: pass a messageId as smtp/send does (route.ts:24-28,138).

'Edit draft' -> Send never sets \Answered: MessageMenu.tsx:255-256 and MessageQuickActions.tsx:62 open compose in mode 'edit', and ComposeOrchestrator.tsx:971-979 only flags reply/replyAll/forward, although composeInitState.ts:402-406 resolves composeReplyMessage. A reply that is started, closed and finished later therefore leaves the original 'unanswered' for the other member.

A manual account-wide sync already exists: TopBar.tsx:443 and FolderPane.tsx:113 call syncAccount(undefined,'new'), which walks every folder including Sent (useSyncController.ts:666-724). feat/ui-shell replaces TopBar.tsx and FolderPane.tsx (TEAM-INBOX.md:705), so the new shell must keep that action or the only manual way for B to pull in A's reply without opening Sent disappears. B's startup sync covers only the active folder (lib/syncPolicy.ts:139-150).

Ownership gap in §9: feat/thread-collaboration owns only 'lib/drafts.ts (hook only)' (TEAM-INBOX.md:706). lib/specialFolders.ts and drafts/save/route.ts are owned by no branch, and MailClient.tsx (handleSendDraft notice at 3199-3203) is partly owned by feat/ui-shell (TEAM-INBOX.md:705). The Sent-copy status, the server-side ingest, the draft concurrency and the \Answered changes all need an explicit ownership amendment before Stage 2 starts.

The proposed server-side ingest of the Sent copy needs a fallback when appendImapMessage returns null (no UIDPLUS, or the Sent folder not selected on the pooled connection; mutations.ts:51-53, imapflow append.js:139-145): UID SEARCH by Message-ID in Sent. Otherwise both the ingest and the recordReplySent thread resolution are skipped silently.

Without UIDPLUS, draft saves fail AFTER a successful APPEND (lib/drafts.ts:255-258). The client gets no draftId, so each autosave retry adds another orphan draft to the shared IMAP Drafts folder, which the other member and other IMAP clients see.
